rule: In a competition week (e.g. CrossFit Open week) run volume is 0.8x the current weekly mileage
summary: No study tests run volume during a multi-week in-season test like the Open. Taper meta-analyses (Bosquet 2007; Wang 2023) say peaking works best with a 41-60% volume cut while intensity and frequency are kept. A 20% cut is therefore a mild 'freshen-up', not a peak, which fits an Open week where one scored workout sits inside normal training. The number is a sensible heuristic. However, the config key is NOT read by code: engine/running.py ramp_targets hardcodes 0.8 for competition weeks, so editing season.yaml does nothing. Proposed: No value change. Code PR: make engine/running.py ramp_targets read season.deload.competition_run_factor instead of the hardcoded 0.8 (pass it through RampRules from plan_block.build_outline), and bump the rule version in engine/audit.py. This is wrong if, after wiring, the simulations change output while the config is still at 0.8.

sources.note: Bosquet 2007, 27 studies: best taper is ~2 wk with volume cut 41-60%, intensity and frequency kept; a 20% cut is well short of a peaking taper
Wang 2023, endurance athletes: tapers that cut volume 41-60% and keep intensity/frequency improved time-trial performance
Vachon 2021, team sports: tapering improves power, VO2max and repeated sprints, but there are too few studies to give a dose for in-season competition
